undated_mentions: 12th-13th centuries: town adhered politically to the Novgorod Republic
14th century: functioned as capital of a de facto sovereign republic
Several years after 1348: veche promulgated the Pskov Charter law code
13th century: German merchants present in Zapskovye
First half of 16th century: Hanseatic trading post in Zapskovye
15th century: Pskov Krom withstood twenty-six sieges
Polish-Lithuanian siege: Stephen Báthory undertook some thirty-one attacks
Peace negotiations after the 1615 defence, culminating in the Treaty of Stolbovo
During World War I: Pskov became a centre of wartime activity behind the lines
Under the military administrator: duties ceded to elected municipal duma; press censorship ended
Soviet era: large parts of the city rebuilt; many ancient churches demolished
